I'm someone who takes my privacy seriously and have for the past few years. I've taken many steps to lock down my computer and online accounts to ensure my privacy is kept intact and generally know how to protect my personal information.

But, I can't help to think that there is something I'm overlooking; some sort of underlying threat to my privacy that I'm not aware of. I'm not well up-to-date in the news since WhoaVerse is probably the only way news can get to me. So, I wanted to ask the WhoaVerse community.

Big or small, what is the biggest threat to privacy today that I'm probably not aware of?
Q: What is the biggest threat to privacy today?

Biggest threat to your privacy are your friends who are ignorant and do not care about privacy. They will upload your photos and other personal information without asking you or without realizing what they are doing. So to sum it up: people who do not care about privacy are the biggest threat to privacy. They are the ones not reacting when privacy is endangered and who, by being silent, enable officials to do whatever they want :)

I have many friends who always give me the "you're weird" look whenever I talk about privacy seriously. Thank you for your answer!

I believe that this mindset is already too strong and it has already allowed officials to do whatever they want. It is a pretty simple human psychology concept, in a differrent context: if only a fraction of people (say 1%) in a country are against or neutral when it comes to racism, racism will flourish there and when people are being racist on the street, that 1% will be unable to do anything to stop it.

The biggest threat to your privacy is two-fold: One is the profit and power motive. Actors such as Google who were funded by power-driven intelligence organizations and who now are required by publicly-traded-corporation status to pursue profits in every way possible. Actors such as the NSA, with a nearly unlimited budget and a stated mission to pursue the destruction of your privacy. These are the institutional threats to privacy.

The second is cultural narcissism which in part derives from the same profit motive by way of Consumerism. This is the desire for people to shape their image and deceive in order to present false fronts. This conformist psychology creates incentives for deception and a hunger for information about others for comparison. These are the drivers in an individual that can spur them to attack privacy.

Beyond that you really just need to worry about lack of care - something that is rapidly going away in the technology context. Who isn't designing their product securely at this point?
I would go further to suggest that an apathetic populace is probably the biggest threat. If the public cared about their privacy, they have the collective political power to secure it.

Everyone in here is being way too specific, IMO. Stupid friends, Google, the NSA, etc are definitely threats to privacy, but they're too specific for me. If you removed just one of any of those from the equation, privacy in the world would still diminish.

I think that the biggest threat to our privacy is the advancements in technology that have been made over the last 100 years.
